events.reason: Motor vehicle collision, lower abdominal pain

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: MVC, seatbelt bruising lower abdomen. Prior splenectomy. Technique: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast, portal venous phase. Findings: Liver normal in size and enhancement. Spleen surgically absent. Gallbladder, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys normal. Small and large bowel normal in caliber without wall thickening. No free fluid. No free air. No mesenteric hematoma. Bladder normal. No fracture.
reports.conclusion: No acute traumatic abnormality in the abdomen or pelvis. Postsplenectomy.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 01/13/2026

29 y/o male, restrained driver in a collision this morning, came in on his own. Lower belly is sore where the seatbelt crossed. No nausea or vomiting. Prior splenectomy after a crash in 2024 and a minor liver injury in 2025, both at the trauma center.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Vitals within normal limits. Awake, comfortable. Band of bruising across the lower abdomen in the seatbelt distribution. Abdomen soft, mildly tender over the bruise, no rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds present. Chest, pelvis and extremities unremarkable.

CBC normal. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast: no acute abnormality.

Impression: seatbelt bruising of the lower abdominal wall after MVC; no intra-abdominal injury on CT.
Discharged home. Return immediately for increasing pain, fever, vomiting or lightheadedness. Follow up with PCP.

reports.text: Upright AP chest. Indication: acute abdominal pain after recent MVC. Findings: Free air beneath the diaphragm. Lungs clear. Heart size normal. No pneumothorax or effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 01/15/2026   Arrival 13:05

CC: severe abdominal pain

HPI: 29M with prior traumatic splenic rupture (splenectomy 10/2024) and blunt abdominal trauma with a suspected liver injury (observed here 5/2025), both from earlier car crashes. Two days ago he was in another collision with a seatbelt mark across the lower abdomen; seen at an outside ED, CT reportedly unremarkable, sent home. About 4 hours ago he had abrupt onset of sharp, constant lower abdominal pain that has gotten steadily worse. Denies nausea or vomiting; bowel habits unchanged.

PSH: exploratory laparotomy with splenectomy 10/2024. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: noncontributory; no bleeding disorders or liver disease. SH: never smoker, social alcohol, sales.

Vitals: BP 100/60, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.8 C.
Exam: uncomfortable, lying still. Abdomen with diffuse tenderness, rebound and guarding; bowel sounds hypoactive. Fading seatbelt bruise across the lower abdomen. Old midline scar.

Labs: WBC 15.0 K/uL, Hgb 13.2 g/dL, lactate 3.5 mmol/L.
Upright chest film: free air under the diaphragm.

Impression: hollow viscus perforation with peritonitis after blunt trauma, most likely small bowel.
ED course: 2 L crystalloid, IV piperacillin-tazobactam, IV analgesia. Surgery at bedside; to OR.

reports.text: Specimen: small intestine, ileum, segmental resection. Gross: segment of small bowel 12 cm in length with stapled ends, a full-thickness defect on the antimesenteric wall and fibrinous exudate on the serosa. Microscopic: transmural defect with acute inflammation and necrosis at the edges; acute fibrinopurulent serositis. Mucosa away from the defect unremarkable. Both stapled margins viable.
reports.conclusion: Small intestine (ileum), resection: transmural perforation with acute serositis. Margins viable.

medications.drug: acetaminophen 325 MG / oxycodone hydrochloride 5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe pain. Dispense 12 tablets.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT - TRAUMA / ACUTE CARE SURGERY
Date of surgery: 01/15/2026

Preoperative diagnosis: pneumoperitoneum and peritonitis after blunt abdominal trauma
Postoperative diagnosis: traumatic perforation of the ileum with secondary peritonitis
Procedure: re-exploratory laparotomy, segmental small-bowel resection with stapled primary anastomosis, abdominal washout
Anesthesia: general

Findings: Enteric contents and fibrinous exudate throughout the lower abdomen and pelvis. Full-thickness perforation of the ileum about 60 cm proximal to the ileocecal valve. Remaining small bowel and colon examined end to end without other injury. Liver unremarkable. Splenic bed clean.

Description: Entry through the prior midline incision. Contamination evacuated and cultures not sent. The injured segment, about 12 cm, was resected with a stapler and a side-to-side functional end-to-end stapled anastomosis created; mesenteric defect closed. Abdomen irrigated with several liters of warm saline until clear. Fascia closed with running looped absorbable suture; skin closed with staples over wicks.

To the floor in stable condition.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - TRAUMA / ACUTE CARE SURGERY
Admitted 01/15/2026   Discharged 01/21/2026

Diagnosis: traumatic perforation of the small intestine (ileum) with secondary peritonitis, 2 days after a seatbelt injury.
Procedure: re-laparotomy, 12 cm ileal resection with primary anastomosis, washout (01/15).
Other: asplenia after splenectomy 10/2024.

Course: Piperacillin-tazobactam IV for 4 days after source control, then stopped. Afebrile from POD2. Diet advanced from POD3 with return of bowel function; tolerating a regular diet on discharge. Walking independently. Wound clean; wicks out POD2. Pathology: transmural perforation with acute serositis, viable margins.

Allergies: NKDA
Discharge medications: acetaminophen-oxycodone 325/5 mg 1 tab every 6 hours as needed for severe pain, #12; acetaminophen otherwise.

Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb until early March. No driving on oxycodone. Staples out at surgery clinic 2/4. PCP within a week. Any fever, vomiting, worsening pain or wound drainage: return.

medications.drug: acetaminophen 325 MG / oxycodone hydrochloride 5 MG Oral Tablet

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Records from both EDs, the op note, pathology and discharge summary came in Friday; reviewed.

Course: MVC 1/13 with a seatbelt bruise, outside ED CT negative, sent home. Two days later sudden severe lower abdominal pain; trauma center found free air and peritonitis; re-laparotomy 1/15 with a 12 cm ileal resection and primary anastomosis for a perforation. 4 days of pip-tazo. Home 1/21.

Today: eating three small meals plus snacks, no nausea. Bowel movements daily, soft. No fevers. Incision tight but improving. Took oxycodone the first two nights home only; acetaminophen since. Down about 4 kg from his usual.

Exam: afebrile, vitals stable, weight 78 kg. Comfortable. Lungs clear, heart regular. Midline incision with staples, clean and dry, no erythema or drainage. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near the wound, not distended, bowel sounds normal.

CBC: WBC 8.4, Hgb 12.6.

A/P
1. Traumatic small-bowel perforation with peritonitis, s/p resection: recovering well. WBC normal. Staples out at surgery clinic 2/4. Eat as tolerated; weight should come back.
2. Pain: off oxycodone; removed from his list.
3. Asplenia: MenB booster was due this month. Holding until he's further out from surgery; nurse visit in March.
4. Work: will message when surgery clears him for desk and driving duties.

documents.title: Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Re: Lucas Wisniewski, DOB 05/06/1996
Acute care surgery clinic, 02/04/2026

Nearly three weeks after re-laparotomy and ileal resection for a traumatic perforation. Eating normally, bowels regular, no fevers. Staples removed; incision healing well with no infection or hernia. I reviewed the pathology with him (transmural perforation, viable margins).

He can go back to work once he feels ready. No lifting over 10 pounds until early March. Off opioids, so driving is fine. Final check in about five weeks.

Acute Care Surgery

documents.title: Back to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Surgery said I can go back whenever I'm ready as long as I don't lift over 10 lbs until March. I'd like to start Monday 2/23. Can you do the same kind of letter as last time? Thanks

documents.title: RE: Back to work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sure - the letter is under Documents, with Monday 2/23 as your start and the 10 lb limit through 3/8. Take it easy the first week if the driving days are long. Nurse visit for your MenB booster is on the books for 3/10.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
MenB booster for asplenia, deferred from January because of his surgery. Afebrile, feels well. Bexsero 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction.

Next MenB booster in 2-3 years; MenACWY booster due January 2030. Recalls updated.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'd like to book my physical for September, mornings are best. Also do I need any shots before then because of the spleen thing?

documents.title: RE: Physical
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Lucas, you're booked Thursday 9/17 at 8:40. Nothing is due before then. We'll give your flu shot at that visit if the fall supply is in. Your MenB booster was done in March and the next one isn't for 2-3 years; the MenACWY booster is due in 2030. Fasting isn't needed for your labs.
